provenance_summary: V1-B biological expansion wave. Algae-derived polysaccharides (alginate, carrageenan, agar) as bio-adsorbents for heavy metals and dyes. Rich in carboxyl and sulfate groups.

mechanisms.name: Alginate gel bead adsorption
mechanisms.description: Sodium alginate cross-linked with Ca²⁺ forms gel beads with carboxyl groups for heavy metal coordination

pollutant_feature.text: Heavy metal ions and cationic dyes

bio_structure.text: Alginate gel bead with carboxyl groups (-COOH)

interaction.text: Ion exchange and coordination with carboxyl groups

why_it_works.text: High density of carboxyl groups provides abundant binding sites

causal_chain.transferable_principle: Alginate gel bead structure provides high density of carboxyl groups for heavy metal coordination and ion exchange

engineering_constraints.description: Alginate extraction from brown algae via alkaline digestion

narrative.text: Algae polysaccharides (alginate, carrageenan, agar) are abundant biopolymers from marine algae. Alginate forms gel beads with Ca²⁺ that have high density of carboxyl groups for heavy metal adsorption.

design_translation.idea: Extract alginate from brown algae and form gel beads for heavy metal and dye removal
examples: Sodium alginate gel bead for Pb²⁺ adsorption
design_translation.applicability: Heavy metal and dye removal from wastewater
